# Substratal Apps — Platform API

> Substratal Apps is the user/organization/tenancy/settings/storage layer an
> app developer would otherwise have to build themselves — comparable in
> shape to Auth0, Clerk, or WorkOS, scoped around everything a multi-tenant
> app needs: accounts, roles and permissions, per-app settings, team/tenancy
> structure, and per-user storage, all behind one API. This site is the
> system of record for that API: users, roles, per-app access (the "turn an
> app on/off for a user" switch), profiles, and settings across every
> Application built on the platform. It is API-first: no user-facing
> interface is specified here — a dashboard for easier onboarding is
> planned, but it is a separate, later client of this API. Billing is each
> Application developer's own concern; this API tracks entitlement state,
> it does not process payments.

This site is the living specification. Treat it as authoritative over any
older single-file draft found elsewhere in the repository's history.

## Start here

- [Home]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/): what Substratal Apps is and how this site is organized.
- [Getting Started]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/getting-started/): the fastest path to understanding the system before writing code against it.
- [Quickstart]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/quickstart/): a runnable curl walkthrough of the core access model.
- [Domain Model]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/domain-model/): the entities — User, Organization, Application, Role, Permission, Entitlement, Profile, Setting, Order, Audit Event.
- [Access Control]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/access-control/): how Entitlement (is the app on?) and Role (what can they do?) combine to decide every request.
- [Database Schema]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/domain-model/database-schema/): Postgres types, constraints, and indexes behind every entity — for implementers, not API callers.

## API reference

- [Conventions]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/conventions/): base URL, auth, pagination, idempotency, error shape, ID format.
- [Auth]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/auth/)
- [Users]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/users/)
- [Profiles]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/profiles/)
- [Settings]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/settings/)
- [Applications]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/applications/)
- [Entitlements]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/entitlements/): the on/off switch for a user's access to an app.
- [Roles & Permissions]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/roles-and-permissions/)
- [Organizations]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/organizations/)
- [Audit]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/audit/)
- [Webhooks]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/webhooks/)
- [API Keys]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/api-reference/api-keys/): service-to-service credentials.
- [openapi.yaml]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/openapi.yaml): the same API surface as a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 document.

## Also useful

- [Workflows]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/workflows/): purchase-to-access, admin revokes access, role changes, end to end.
- [Trust Model]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/trust-model/): how a separately-hosted downstream app verifies a user's access against this API.
- [Non-Functional Requirements]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/non-functional-requirements/)
- [Compliance & Data Protection]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/compliance/): which of SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA apply, and when.
- [Roadmap]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/roadmap/): MVP through Phase 3.
- [Deployment Architecture]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/deployment-architecture/): the cost-capped first deployment on AWS, and the path to scale.
- [Decisions]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/decisions/): the open questions this spec depends on, and their status.
- [Changelog]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/changelog/): what's changed in this spec over time.
- [Glossary]({{ site.url }}{{ site.baseurl }}/glossary/)
